summary: Onset ~13:20 UTC. pricing-engine p99 jumped 60ms -> ~2.1s and market-data-service p99 40ms -> ~1.85s, both in lockstep, with no deploy to either service. The fault originates in the shared redis-cache: at 13:22:10 node redis-cache-2 failed health checks and was marked down; at 13:22:52 a replica (redis-cache-3) was promoted whose dataset was EMPTY. redis-cache memory_pct collapsed 70%->8.6% and hit_ratio_pct 96%->15% at 13:20, confirming the cache contents were lost. market-data-service, now getting ~15% cache hits, rebuilds each quote from the exchange feed snapshot (2-8.7s each), which drives its CPU to 79-94% and propagates multi-second quote latency up through pricing-engine to trading screens. exchange-gateway and redis-cache CPU remain flat/noisy-healthy; no config or code change involved. Best hypothesis: infrastructure_failure at redis-cache (empty-replica failover), matching HIST-107.

ranked_hypotheses.title: redis-cache primary failure promoted an empty replica; cold-cache storm overwhelms market-data-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The redis primary (redis-cache-2) failed health checks and was marked down at ~13:22; the promoted replica (redis-cache-3) had an empty dataset (was mid-resync). All cached quotes were lost, so market-data-service fell back to rebuilding every quote from the exchange feed snapshot in 2-8.7s, saturating its CPU (79-94%) and raising quote latency, which propagated to pricing-engine and trading screens.

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache primary fails health checks and is marked down
replica promoted with an empty dataset -> hit ratio 96%->15%, memory 70%->8.6%
market-data-service catches cache-miss storm, rebuilds quotes from exchange feed (2-8.7s each)
market-data-service CPU rises to 79-94% and p99 to ~1.85s
pricing-engine quote computation deadline exceeded, p99 ~2.1s, visible on trading screens

assumptions: redis-cache is the shared cache both market-data-service and pricing-engine depend on (confirmed by dependency graph)
the health-check failure was an operational fault rather than an externally-triggered event

ranked_hypotheses.title: market-data-service capacity saturation from its own resource limits
ranked_hypotheses.statement: market-data-service hit a capacity/resource ceiling (CPU saturation) causing quote rebuilds to queue and slow down, independent of redis.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate is flat ~950 req/s (F12) so load did not grow; the CPU spike is fully explained by cold-cache rebuilds (F4/F7); and the cache hit-ratio/memory collapse plus empty-replica failover is an upstream cause, not a consequence of market-data saturation.

ranked_hypotheses.title: exchange-gateway / external exchange feed degradation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The upstream exchange feed provider degraded, slowing quote rebuilds at market-data-service.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: exchange-gateway latency_p99 (~130ms) and upstream_latency_ms (~120ms) are flat across onset (F10); the rebuild slowness only appears because of cache misses, not a slow feed.

facts.statement: pricing-engine p99 rose from ~60ms to ~2.1s at 13:20 UTC.
market-data-service p99 rose from ~40ms to ~1.85s at the same 13:20 bucket.
pricing-engine errors attribute the slowness to market-data-service (deadline exceeded, 'market-data-service took ...ms').
market-data-service logged a cache-miss storm rebuilding quotes from the exchange feed for 2-8.7s.
redis-cache memory_pct fell from ~70% to ~8.6%, indicating the dataset was emptied.
redis-cache raised an empty-replica failover: primary marked down, replica with empty dataset promoted.
redis-cache evictions stayed ~3/min and CPU ~22% (no eviction/reaper involvement).
market-data-service CPU rose to 79-94% during the event.
exchange-gateway latency and upstream latency stayed flat (~130ms / ~120ms).
No deployments or config changes on 2026-04-09 for pricing-engine, market-data-service, or redis-cache.
market-data-service restarts stayed 0 and memory flat (~62%).
Historical incident HIST-107 had identical symptoms and root cause (redis failover promoted empty replica).

timeline.event: Last normal bucket: pricing-engine p99 ~60ms, market-data p99 ~40ms, redis hit ratio ~96%.
exchange-gateway logs a trivial 38ms clock drift / NTP resync.
redis-cache hit_ratio collapses to ~15% and memory_pct to ~8.6%; market-data p99 jumps to 1433ms and CPU to 79%; pricing-engine p99 jumps to 1697ms.
redis-cache-2 fails health check (3 PING timeouts) and is marked primary-down.
market-data-service begins logging cache miss storm rebuilds from exchange feed.
Replica redis-cache-3 promoted to primary with an EMPTY dataset (was resyncing).
pricing-engine errors 'quote computation deadline exceeded' begin.
redis-cache client reconnect storm (15048 new connections/10s) as clients reconnect post-failover.
Still degraded; pricing-engine p99 ~1164ms, market-data p99 ~912ms, redis hit ratio ~47% (slowly warming).

recommended_actions.action: Trigger/verify a cache warm-up (pre-populate hot quotes in redis-cache) to restore hit ratio and drain the rebuild backlog instead of waiting for organic warming.
recommended_actions.rationale: Current state is a slow self-healing cold-cache storm; active warming restores quotes fastest.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm the correct/full replica to promote or resync redis-cache from a non-empty source; verify redis-cache-3 was in fact empty and check replication/sync configuration.
recommended_actions.rationale: The trigger was promotion of an empty replica; ensure no further failovers occur and data is not served from an empty store.

recommended_actions.action: Investigate why redis-cache-2 failed health checks (3 consecutive PING timeouts) - host/network saturation, blocked event loop, or persistence (background save) stalls.
recommended_actions.rationale: Root trigger is the primary node failing health checks; background saves were active and memory had been ~70%.

recommended_actions.action: Add replica-sync readiness gating so a replica mid-resync is never promoted to primary with an empty dataset.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence of the exact HIST-107 failure mode (cold cache storm after empty-replica failover).

recommended_actions.action: Decouple quote serving from cache-fill: add request coalescing / single-flight and backpressure when rebuilding from the exchange feed, so misses cannot saturate CPU.
recommended_actions.rationale: The amplification came from every miss independently rebuilding (2-8.7s) and saturating market-data CPU.

data_gaps: First query_metrics attempt for market-data-service latency returned 503 (tc-007); a retry succeeded (tc-012) so coverage is complete, but this hints at transient telemetry backend instability.
The very first get_deployments call was partial (tc-003); the retried full query (tc-006) showed only the unrelated auth-service deploy, so no deploy evidence is missing.
No infra/node-level telemetry for the redis-cache host (only redis app metrics) is available, so the underlying reason redis-cache-2 stopped answering PINGs cannot be confirmed from these tools.
No metric explains advertised pricing-engine 'deadline exceeded' threshold value; taken from logs only.

findings.statement: pricing-engine p99 latency was flat ~59-61ms until 13:12, then jumped to 1697ms at the 13:20 bucket and peaked at 2309.91ms.
market-data-service p99 latency was flat ~40ms until 13:12, then jumped to 1433.5ms at the 13:20 bucket, matching the pricing-engine onset.

pricing-engine logs are dominated by 192 ERROR lines 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' starting 13:23:57, pinpointing market-data-service as the slow downstream hop.

refs.quote: quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took 5171ms

findings.statement: market-data-service logs show 289 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot (<n>ms)' warnings starting 13:22:25, with rebuilds taking up to ~8748ms.

refs.quote: cache miss storm: quote:84685 not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot (6864ms)

findings.statement: redis-cache hit_ratio_pct collapsed from ~96% to ~15% at the 13:20 bucket and stayed low, recovering only slowly.
redis-cache memory_pct collapsed from ~70% to ~8.6% at the 13:20 bucket, indicating the cached dataset was emptied, not merely evicted under pressure.

redis-cache logs show the primary node failed health checks and an EMPTY replica was promoted: 'node redis-cache-2 failed health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts); marking primary as down' at 13:22:10 and 'failover: promoting replica redis-cache-3 to primary; dataset on new primary is empty (replica was resyncing)' at 13:22:52.

refs.quote: node redis-cache-2 failed health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts); marking primary as down
failover: promoting replica redis-cache-3 to primary; dataset on new primary is empty (replica was resyncing)

findings.statement: redis-cache evictions_per_min stayed flat around 3/min through the event (no eviction-driven key loss), and redis-cache cpu_pct stayed ~22%.
market-data-service CPU jumped from ~45% to 79-94% at the 13:20 bucket, consistent with CPU spent rebuilding quotes after cache misses.
exchange-gateway (market-data's upstream exchange provider) is healthy and flat: latency_p99 ~130ms and upstream_latency_ms ~120ms unchanged across the onset.
No deployments or config/flag changes exist for pricing-engine, market-data-service, or redis-cache on 2026-04-09 (only an unrelated auth-service v7.2.0 at 11:30).
market-data-service request_rate stayed flat ~950 req/s across the onset, so the failure is not a traffic/load surge.
redis-cache logs show 'client reconnect storm: 15048 new connections in 10s' at 13:30:20 (later 92851) and full resync events, consistent with clients reconnecting after the failover.

refs.quote: client reconnect storm: 15048 new connections in 10s

findings.statement: market-data-service restarts metric stayed 0 throughout, and memory_pct stayed flat ~62% (no restart/OOM).
Historical post-mortem HIST-107 (2025-12-09) records 'Cold cache storm after redis failover' with root cause 'Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica', same services and symptoms.

refs.quote: Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica

findings.statement: The simultaneous onset (13:20) of redis-cache hit-ratio/memory collapse, market-data-service latency/CPU spike, and pricing-engine latency spike, combined with the empty-replica failover log at 13:22, establishes an infrastructure failure at redis-cache as the origin, with market-data-service and pricing-engine as downstream victims.
